verses.text: "Go ahead and call out. Will anyone answer you? Which of the holy ones will you turn to?
Resentment kills the fool, and jealousy kills the simple.
I've seen a fool take root, but I quickly called his home cursed.
His children are far from safety. They're crushed at the city gate, with no one to rescue them.
The hungry eat up his harvest, taking it even from among the thorns. A trap stands open for everything they own.
Suffering doesn't come out of the dust, and trouble doesn't sprout from the ground.
People are born into trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
If it were me, I'd seek God and put my case in his hands.
He does great things beyond understanding, more wonders than anyone can count.
He gives rain to the earth and sends water over the fields.
He lifts up those who've been brought low and raises those who mourn to safety.
He ruins the plans of the crafty so they can't carry out what they've set out to do.
He catches the wise in their own schemes, and the plans of the cunning collapse.
They run into darkness in broad daylight and grope at noon as if it were night.
But God rescues the needy from words that cut like swords and from the grip of the powerful.
So the poor have hope, and injustice has to shut its mouth.
Look, how fortunate is the person God corrects. So don't despise the Almighty's discipline.
He wounds, and he dresses the wound. He injures, and his own hands heal.
He'll rescue you from six troubles. Even in seven, no harm will touch you.
In famine he'll save you from death, and in war he'll save you from the sword.
You'll be sheltered from the lash of the tongue, and you won't fear destruction when it comes.
You'll laugh at destruction and famine and won't be afraid of wild animals.
Even the stones in the field will be at peace with you, and the wild animals will leave you unharmed.
You'll know your tent is secure. When you check your fold, nothing will be missing.
You'll see your descendants grow numerous, like the grass of the earth.
You'll come to your grave at a ripe old age, like a bundle of grain gathered in its season.
We've looked into this and found it true. Listen to it and take it to heart for your own good."
